title: Aspiring writer-director here. Help me with something!

commenti.body:
The second premise sounds interesting but if I were at the theater and had to buy tickets, Somewhere With Elephants would seem like the safer bet. 

Garden of Whispers is obviously trying to be very deep and poetic which means there's a much higher likelihood that it'll turn out botched somehow.

Latenight armchair movie enjoyer, so don't take my comments too seriously. 


I'm partial to the second plot. The first one seems a little too familiar, well-trodden. Even before you list your inspirations, the synopsis brings those films to mind. This isn't inherently a bad thing but can lead to a situation where your film is constantly drawing comparisons to other works, making it harder to stand on its own.  

The second synopsis is a more initially engaging and unique imo. It's quite distinct from the style and narrative form of contemporary films, which makes it stand out a lot more. I do have a few concerns though. For it to be successful, it would have to balance a level of subtly that prevents the revelation from being too obvious or too straightforward without being frustratingly cryptic. I also think it would be important to pick your poems wisely and find an interesting way to transition from one poem to the next. 

Just my thoughts.
